findings.text: openspec:fix-cochange-tools-on-postgres and openspec:add-recurrent-tree-indexing both edit the same function, `index_tree` in packages/cli/src/mintmory/cli/main.py. The first inserts a guard at about :550-551 and changes the co-change report rows. The second changes the text-content eligibility at about :613-617, adds counters at about :584-591 and adds a report row. Both units have depends_on [] and cite line numbers from the same staging commit. Run unattended, they will conflict or shift each other's line anchors. The plan states no ordering or merge rule. The report table is also edited by both, and each unit's scenarios assert on its rows.

deployment-hardening tasks 1.4, 4.1 and 4.2 ask for `docker build`, `helm lint` and `helm template` plus kubeconform, and for a live `/healthz` 200. Section 5 itself says helm, docker and the network are not guaranteed on the runner. Section 1-4 tasks are shown unchecked, even though the text says they shipped in 317e0bf. An implementer cannot tell whether to redo them (for example re-commit uv.lock or rewrite the Dockerfile) or skip them. Only section 5 is the real work, and the task list does not mark that boundary. The same applies to add-recurrent-tree-indexing section 1, which lists seven items as 'already implemented'.

add-recurrent-tree-indexing contains drafts that contradict its proposal and specs. design.md says it is 'proposed', defines a default artifact denylist, and specifies launchd, `--once` and `--install-agent`. gaps.md says four decisions are still 'required before implementation'. The proposal says those decisions are taken, the status is IMPLEMENTED, and there is no default denylist. The proposal says it and specs/ win, but design.md and gaps.md remain in the change folder. An implementer reading them could add `--once`, `--install-agent` or a denylist. The folder should be pruned or marked superseded.

Every unit's gate runs `npx --yes @fission-ai/openspec@1.14.1 validate ... --strict`, which needs network access. deployment-hardening section 5 says the network is not guaranteed. The plan does not say whether this gate is optional when the network is absent.

The two helm-based selector tests in deployment-hardening are skipped when `helm` is missing. In that case only the text-based checks of the helper and templates run. The postgres PDB scenario also assumes `values-postgres.yaml` renders with only the listed `--set` flags. The material does not show that, so a required postgres value could make `helm template` fail.

fix-distiller-prompt-cap relies on `_insert_elision_markers(lines, kept_sorted, 0)`, whose third argument is not described. It also relies on which indices count as 'protected' or 'droppable' in the existing code ('exactly as today'). The implementer must infer both from the current source, and the `_render` helper's behaviour depends on them.

The `scripts/bump_version.py` change (task 5.6) is tested only through `bump_chart_text`. The spec claim that `bump_version.py X.Y.Z` rewrites the Chart file, which `main()` is meant to do, has no test.

openspec:add-local-observability-stack depends only on add-telemetry-runtime. Its docs and README rely on part 2 output. The README gives the Prometheus query `histogram_quantile(... mintmory_search_latency_ms_bucket ... by phase)`. Task 4.2 tells the reader to open the `mintmory.search.*` children in Jaeger. Both exist only after add-telemetry-heavy-path-spans. Part 3's `gen_ai.chat` CLIENT span is also named in the guide. The unit's depends_on should list add-telemetry-heavy-path-spans, and probably boundary-tracing. Otherwise the guide could be written and merged before the spans and metrics it describes exist.

Part 4's doctor state values (`exporting`, `off`, `no collector`, `SDK missing`) are mapped from part 1's `_resolve_state`. Task 2.2 states only `export` -> `exporting`. It does not state `sdk missing` -> `SDK missing`. It also does not say which endpoint the doctor row shows when a per-signal `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT` is set. The spec says only 'the trace endpoint'.

The command span name rule in part 2 is 'mintmory.cli.<command> (spaces become dots)'. For `history backfill` this gives `mintmory.cli.history.backfill`. The runtime unit's CLI callback refers to the group as `history`, and no scenario pins the nested-command name. Only `index-tree`, `ingest` and `add` are tested, so the nested names are unverified.

Parts 2, 3 and 4 all edit `docs/OBSERVABILITY.md` (sections 4.3/4.4, a new subsection, and 4.5 plus the section 4 summary). Parts 2, 3 and 4 also all edit `telemetry.py` and `cli/main.py`. The edits do not overlap in content, but part 4's rewrite of section 4 could overwrite or contradict the part 2 and part 3 text if the order is not enforced. The dependency fix above would enforce it.

The prerequisite openspec:add-recurrent-tree-indexing is marked IMPLEMENTED but still has an open gap (the online-only guard on the text pass, per its proposal). Its tasks.md was not shown to me. Part 2's index-tree spans and counts (`scanned`, `converted`, `pruned`) assume that command's current behaviour, which I could not check.

The proposal says it relies on parts 1 to 3 ('Parts 1 to 3 make MintMory export…'). But depends_on lists only add-telemetry-runtime (part 1). The deliverables use content that parts 2 and 3 add. The README query uses `mintmory_search_latency_ms_bucket` with a `phase` label. The guide tells the reader to read `mintmory.search.*` child spans. Neither is defined in part 1, whose non-goals say new spans and metrics belong to parts 2 and 3. If those units are in the plan, they must be in depends_on. If they are not, the documented metric and span names cannot be verified.

The doctor row is under-specified. 'Trace endpoint' is not defined for the configured case. It could be OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT as given, the per-signal TRACES variable, or the endpoint with /v1/traces appended. The default case must show `http://localhost:4318`, but only that case is pinned. Neither the spec nor the tasks say which URL `reachable` probes, nor which default service name is shown (e.g. `mintmory-cli`). The mapping from `_resolve_state` to display text covers only `export` -> `exporting`. The spec says `SDK missing` while part 1 returns `sdk missing`. The exact output format of the row (labels and separators) is not fixed, so tests can only match substrings.

The `mintmory-api` compose service depends on facts the implementer is told to look up in the Dockerfile: the data path, the command, and the DB env var. Nothing says the image installs the `otel` extra. If it does not, `MINTMORY_OTEL_ENABLED=true` leaves telemetry off (state 'sdk missing') and the profile does not deliver traces. No test or scenario covers this. The pinned image tags (collector 0.162.0, jaeger 2.22.0, prometheus v3.15.0) cannot be checked from the material. The claim that the collector config was validated is not reproducible in the gates, which have no Docker.

Part 1 makes a Typer callback initialise telemetry before every command except serve and mcp-serve. That includes `doctor`. The part 4 task says `telemetry.status` works 'without initialising anything'. The two are compatible only if `status` is a pure read. The interaction (doctor itself may start exporters and spans) is not addressed.

The Helm requirement states what is rendered when `otel.enabled` is true (sampler, sampler arg, resource attributes), but the spec has only a 'Disabled means disabled' scenario. The enabled case is covered only in the tasks, and the helm-based test is skipped when helm is absent. The `mintmory-api` environment `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=mintmory-api` appears in the tasks but not in the spec's requirement or scenario. The guide must name every variable 'MintMory reads', but the test checks only 11 names. Part 1 also reads OTEL_PROPAGATORS, OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG, the OTLP timeout variables and OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS (headers are mentioned in task 4.2).

The unit edits the Helm files configmap.yaml, values.yaml and values.schema.json. The proposal notes that the deployment-hardening change touches other Helm files and may merge first ('rebase if it merges first'). The plan does not state the order or a dependency between the two, so a conflict is possible in an unattended run.

design.md still describes a default artifact denylist, launchd recurrence, `--once` and `--install-agent`. proposal.md and specs/ say these are out of scope or opt-in. design.md has a note saying the proposal and specs win, so an implementer can resolve it, but the stale text could mislead one.

tasks.md section 1 lists seven items as 'already implemented' with checkboxes, and the harness shows them unchecked. An automatic implementer might re-implement or churn working code. The unit's real scope is only section 2, and the document does not say 'do not touch section 1' explicitly.

The counter rule is `text_candidate and online_only and not want_binary`. If `--content` makes the file a binary candidate but the budget is exhausted, the file falls back to metadata and is not counted in `text-skipped-online-only`. No scenario covers this case, so the behaviour is implied, not decided.

A file that was indexed as content while local and is later reported online-only is not addressed. It is unchanged by size and mtime, so it would be skipped and keep its content memories. The spec does not say whether the guard applies when a changed online-only file is re-indexed, apart from the 'metadata only' wording.

The third test (`--content --content-types txt`) may depend on markitdown being installed, since the `docs` extra is not always synced. The tasks do not say whether `.txt` goes through markitdown or plain read, or that the test should inject the fake-markitdown. Line numbers are pinned to staging a08aee3 and may drift.

Several requirements that tasks.md tests have no scenario in the spec. These are the unhandled-exception case (status ERROR and `error.type`), the failing MCP tool, the `OllamaEmbedder` and `OpenAIEmbedder` header injection, and `tracestate` and `baggage` injection. The tasks name the tests, but not the route that raises or the exact assertions. An implementer can still build them, but the spec does not pin them.

Two details of the HTTP middleware are left open. The first is how `OTEL_PYTHON_EXCLUDED_URLS` regexes are matched: `search` or `match`, and against the path or the full URL. The second is how the `http.server.request.duration` metric is labelled when no route matched, because `http.route` is absent. The tasks say only that the span name falls back to `<METHOD>`.

The scenario 'Route template, not the raw path, names the span' says no attribute value contains the id. It does not say whether that covers only the server span or every exported span. The 'Telemetry carries no content' requirement in part 2 allows memory identifiers on other spans, so core spans may legitimately carry the id.

The API lifespan calls `shutdown_telemetry()` when the `TestClient` block exits. The metric scenario does not say whether the in-memory reader is read inside or after that block, and reading after shutdown may return nothing. The spec also does not say whether each retry of an outbound LLM request carries `traceparent`.

Proposal says command spans cover "Long CLI commands" and index-tree gets phase spans, and the spec's CLI list includes `migrate-storage`, `vision-run`, `history backfill`, `history sync`. The unit's Impact lists only main.py, but the history spans are placed in `history/ingest.py` (task 5.2) while the CLI wrapper also exists, so two roots (`mintmory.cli.history.backfill` and `mintmory.history.backfill`) are created. The spec requires only the CLI root; the extra `mintmory.history.*` spans appear only in tasks, not in the spec, so they have no testable requirement.

The requirements for `vision-run`, `migrate-storage`, `history backfill`/`history sync` command spans and for `mintmory.vision.caption`, `mintmory.convert` in `ingest`, `mintmory.index_tree.cochange` and `mintmory.memories.added` on Postgres have no scenario. The only CLI scenarios cover index-tree and ingest failure. The dream concurrent summary test (5.1) is a task with no spec scenario. The conversion/caption spans' attributes (`mintmory.outcome` values) are not enumerated, so tests cannot decide them.

`mintmory.outcome` values, the exact `mintmory.files.*` and other count attribute names for commands other than index-tree, the `graph` phase semantics, and the `mintmory.embed.provider` values for each embedder are not fixed. `provider` and `model` metric attribute names versus `mintmory.embed.provider` and `gen_ai.request.model` span attributes are inconsistent without explanation. The `search_phase` helper's behaviour when `set_count` is not called, and that `command_span` takes the name with spaces replaced by dots, are only partly stated.

No statement on what happens when a phase block raises (does the span get ERROR status; is latency recorded), when the embedder raises, or when the Postgres search paths cannot be run. The embed re-entrancy ContextVar behaviour with threads is unspecified. Task 2.1 says Postgres assertions are added "if they can run", leaving Postgres coverage unverified in the automatic run.

The unit modifies `index_tree` and `ingest` in cli/main.py and relies on the co-change non-SQLite skip (fix-cochange-tools-on-postgres), which is listed. The prerequisite add-recurrent-tree-indexing tasks.md was not shown, so whether `--vision` inline captions and `--prune` exist as the tasks assume cannot be confirmed from the material.

The unit touches telemetry, both storage backends, embedder, history ingest, dreaming, conversion and CLI commands, plus docs. It is large but plausibly one unit. The tasks reference `dreaming.py` and `llm.py` and `record_value`, `add_count`, `_instrument` helpers that this review cannot confirm exist (the prerequisite's task list was truncated).

Acceptance profile is "all" but the privacy test only exercises add, search and a light dream; CLI, embed, conversion and history spans are not covered by the sentinel test, so the no-content rule is not shown across the new spans.

Spec says the 'Auto with no collector stays off' scenario holds when 'nothing listens on the default endpoint' and the test must run in a fresh process, but tasks 3.1 patch `_endpoint_reachable` inside the subprocess script. Meanwhile the proposal says existing tests rely on nothing listening on 4318. The scenario text does not state the patch, so the spec and the test plan describe different preconditions.

'Unreachable collector logs once' requires 'exactly one WARNING about the trace export' while 'three export cycles fail'. Metric export failures are also guarded and warned per signal. The scenario doesn't say how metrics are handled (e.g. metrics disabled or the check limited to the trace logger). It also doesn't say how an implementer should force three cycles deterministically. Task 4.4 sets the OTLP logger to CRITICAL, but the spec's assertion that no `opentelemetry` logger emits WARNING+ is fragile with caplog, because caplog handlers sit on the root logger and the level is set on the parent logger. The behaviour is implementable but the test is under-specified.

The 'Unreachable collector does not slow the caller' requirement (200 spans in under 0.5 s) is a timing assertion with no rule for CI variance. Likewise 'returns within timeout_s plus 0.5 s' relies on the daemon-thread join. If the join times out, the providers are still marked disabled, and the shutdown thread may keep running and be killed at interpreter exit. Pending-span loss in that case is not specified.

The enablement-state function `_resolve_state` and its return strings are fixed in the tasks, but the spec for `settings.enabled` is ambiguous on invalid values: what does `MINTMORY_OTEL_ENABLED=banana` do? Validation failure at settings load would crash the CLI callback. The behaviour of `load_settings()` failing in the CLI callback is also not stated. The 'any case and booleans' mapping is given, but the error value for others is not.

Several failure cases are unstated: a malformed `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` entry (no '='), an unknown `OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER` value (e.g. 'zipkin'), an invalid `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER`, or a malformed endpoint URL given to `_endpoint_reachable` (host/port parsing, https default port, IPv6). Exceptions from `init_telemetry` could crash the CLI, because the spec only says export never raises, not that init never raises.

Concurrency of `init_telemetry` (e.g. FastMCP or threads calling it) and a second init after a failed init are only partly specified. There is no lock. 'A call that returns False leaves no state behind' has no scenario.

Task 8.2 and 4.4 depend on private SDK internals (`trace._TRACER_PROVIDER_SET_ONCE`, `metrics._internal._METER_PROVIDER_SET_ONCE`, `inner._preferred_temporality`, a CRITICAL level on the exporter logger). They are pinned to 1.42.1 but are fragile. Also, setting the logger to CRITICAL hides real SDK errors from users. The spec's claim that the level is restored only on `reset_telemetry` conflicts with a global suppression of exporter diagnostics.

Several requirements have no scenario: `OTEL_PROPAGATORS` default and override, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT` precedence over the generic one, the export timeout default of 3 s and the OTLP timeout variable override, `none` for traces, the CLI skipping `serve` and `mcp-serve`, and that the API lifespan calls shutdown before closing the store (partly covered by the deployment scenario).

The proposal says the console exporter fix for MCP stdio and `auto` mode 'does not import the SDK', yet the CLI callback and API call `load_settings()`/`init_telemetry` on every command, and `_resolve_state` can probe localhost:4318 with a 100 ms connect on every CLI invocation. This adds up to 100 ms latency only when nothing answers (refused connections return at once), which is acceptable but unstated. The deployment scenario also still says 'OTel activates when enabled' without the exporter-selection details.

The proposal says `service.name` follows 'standard precedence', but the spec places `MINTMORY_OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` after the `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` `service.name`. This is consistent, but the settings field `service_name` is described as `None` by default, while the proposal describes the default as `mintmory`. The change is stated in the tasks only.

design.md section 2 still specifies the metadata-action tags `type=ref,event=tag` and has no `flavor: latest=false`. The delta spec and tasks 5.3 forbid `type=ref,event=tag` and require `type=semver,pattern={{version}}` plus `latest=false`. The design also gives the publish job no tag trigger. An implementer who reads the design as authoritative builds the wrong tag scheme. The design should be updated or marked superseded.

The unit scope is ambiguous. tasks.md says sections 1–4 already shipped in 317e0bf, yet they are listed as open tasks. Some of them are not decidable or doable in an automatic run: 1.4 and 4.2 need docker build and a /healthz check, 3.1 says to 'pick one' of two options, and 1.1 says 'the orchestrator commits uv.lock'. The material does not say which tasks the implementer must perform. It should state that only section 5 is in scope, or mark 1–4 as verify-only.

Task 5.8 requires `npx --yes @fission-ai/openspec@1.14.1 validate ...`, which needs network access. Section 5 itself says the network is not guaranteed on the runner. The ruff, mypy and pytest gates are fine. The openspec validation needs a fallback, or it should be excluded from the unattended gates.

The requirement that all OIDC inputs be present has no scenario. Task 5.5 notes that `oauth2proxy-secret.yaml` calls `fail` when the three OIDC values are missing. The failure on missing issuer, client ID or client secret, and the error message, are not specified or tested. The schema enum rejection of an invalid `auth.mode` also has no scenario.

The upgrade hazard is only documented in the README. A release already running oauth2proxy mode must delete its Deployment before `helm upgrade`, because the selector is immutable. No chart-level guard or test covers this. Also, `cookieSecret` is chart-generated with `randAlphaNum` on every render, so it changes on each upgrade. The design does not address this.

The helm-based selector tests are skipped when `helm` is absent. In that case the disjoint-selector behaviour is checked only by text-matching tests. These tests assert exact include counts and exact strings, so they are brittle. This is acceptable because the CI render step adds coverage.

tasks 2.5 says to import SqliteBackend as _SqliteBackend 'if not already imported in that scope'. The path, `mintmory.core.storage`, is given, but whether the name already exists in `index_tree` is left to the implementer. This is harmless because the task tells them to check.

The index-tree scenario requires output to contain both 'co-change skipped' and 'co-change is SQLite-only'. Rich console wrapping could split these strings. The cli_db fixture sets COLUMNS=200, which covers this, but the spec does not say so. The notice is meant to be 'one line', and no test checks that.

The spec does not say what happens with a `--cochange` flag on a non-SQLite store when co-change is disabled by default config. The CLI scenario covers only the flag-on case. Behavior is still clear from the code: the notice prints only when `run_cochange` is true.

The spec says the cap holds 'for every input', but it doesn't say what happens when max_prompt_chars is zero, negative or smaller than the marker. In task 2.5, `avail` can go negative, and then `lines[0][:h]` slices with a negative index. The final `[:max_prompt_chars]` slice still keeps the bound, so the result is safe but untested.

The last scenario's overhead formula assumes `HISTORY_SEGMENT_PROMPT.format(prev_context, transcript, repo)` takes exactly those three placeholders. It also assumes `distill_llm` adds nothing else to the prompt. Neither is visible in the material, so the implementer has to confirm both.

Task 2.1 relies on `_insert_elision_markers(lines, kept_sorted, 0)`. The meaning of the third argument is not stated in the spec. The implementer must read the existing code to check that 0 is correct.

The spec says the function SHALL stay idempotent. The algorithm in tasks 2.2 removes comments from unfenced runs after the fence mask is computed. Comment removal can therefore create a fence line that the first pass did not see. For example, `"<!-- c -->```
<!-- x -->



y  "` becomes a line that is just "```". A second pass then treats it as an opening fence and leaves what follows untouched, so the second pass changes the output. The spec does not say how to handle this, for example by detecting fences before comment removal and leaving such lines alone. The scenarios don't cover it, and the idempotency test only loops over the listed inputs.

The requirement says fenced lines are copied byte-identical. Task 2.2 step 4 ends with `.strip("\n")` over the whole output. For an unterminated fence that ends in blank lines, or a document that begins or ends with a fence, this strips newlines that are inside the fence. The spec doesn't say whether this is allowed. The 'unterminated fence … returns the input unchanged' scenario only avoids the case because its input ends in 'b'.

The fence grammar scenario puts four inputs in one test. There is no scenario for a backtick opener whose info string contains a backtick (e.g. "``` a`b"), or for a closing fence with trailing spaces or tabs. Both are in the grammar but nothing decides them.

The bounds scenario sets the same variable value 5 for both names but is written as a single combined scenario with 'or'. The task list says one test per scenario, so the implementer must cover both names (and the field-name construction) in a single test. This is decidable, just slightly compressed.
The spec does not state what happens when MINTMORY_NOTE_BONUS is set to a non-numeric value, or when it is set empty. Pydantic's default validation error applies, so this is low risk.

The task allows either populate_by_name=True or validate_by_name=True. Both give the same observable behavior, so this is harmless. The 'verified' claims about pydantic behavior are the author's, and I cannot confirm them. The scenarios would catch a mismatch.
